memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But the men who had gone up with him said, "We can't attack those people; they are stronger than we are." And they spread among the Israelites a bad report about the land they had explored. They said, "The land we explored devours those living in it. All the people we saw there are of great size." — Num 13:31-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The ten spies push back hard against Caleb: "We can't." And then they do something worse than express their own fear — they "spread among the Israelites a bad report." Fear, like faith, is contagious. What began as ten frightened hearts soon infected an entire nation.

Notice how their fear grew in the telling. At first they simply said the people were strong. Now the land itself "devours those living in it," and everyone is "of great size." Fear exaggerates. It takes real difficulties and inflates them until they blot out the sky. The more the spies talked, the bigger the giants became in their imagination.

This is how unbelief works in us too. We rehearse our worries, and each time we tell the story the problem grows. We share our fears with others, and soon a whole family or fellowship is discouraged. Words have power — the ten men's report would shape the destiny of a generation, and not for good.

We must be careful what report we spread. Do our words build faith in others or feed their fears? When we speak, do we make God seem large and the obstacles small, or the reverse? The tongue can spread a "bad report" that poisons a community, or it can strengthen weary hearts. Let us be people whose words point others to the faithfulness of God rather than to the size of the giants.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do your words tend to build faith in others or spread fear?
2. How has fear exaggerated a problem in your own mind recently?
3. What "bad report" might you need to stop rehearsing and repeating?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, guard my tongue from spreading fear and discouragement. Help me to speak words that build faith and point others to Your greatness. Let my words strengthen rather than weaken those around me. Amen.
